핵심이슈.summary:
## 오늘의 한국 경제 흐름 요약

소비 측면에서는 1분기 카드 승인액이 322조 원으로 전년 대비 7.2% 증가하며 온라인 쇼핑과 여행 선예약 수요가 소비 회복을 이끌고 있다. 그러나 부동산 시장은 서울 아파트 매매·전세 상승률이 소폭 둔화되고 강남·용산 등 주요 지역에서는 매매가가 하락하는 등 과열이 진정되는 분위기다. 한편 건설 공사비가 중동 전쟁 여파로 7개월 연속 최고치를 경신하고 있고, 종전 이후에도 전략 비축유 확대 움직임으로 고유가가 지속될 것이라는 전망이 나오면서 **비용 인플레이션** 압력이 여전히 높은 상황이다. 금융 시장에서는 신용융자 잔고가 사상 최대치를 기록하자 한국투자·NH·KB증권이 잇따라 신용 규제를 강화하며 과열 경보를 울렸고, 채권 시장은 금리 인하 기대라는 '원군'을 기다리며 관망세를 이어가고 있다. 종합하면, 소비 회복세는 뚜렷하지만 고유가·고공사비 등 공급발 물가 부담과 금융 레버리지 과열이 동시에 진행되는 **엇갈린 경제 신호**가 오늘의 핵심 흐름이다.

key_headlines.title: LG Energy Solution Secures 10 Trillion Won BMW Battery Supply Contract
key_headlines.summary: LG Energy Solution announced a 10 trillion won contract to supply cylindrical batteries for BMW's next-generation electric vehicles, marking a major turnaround for Korean battery makers facing market challenges.

key_headlines.title: Seoul Apartment Jeonse-to-Monthly Rent Conversion Accelerates, Monthly Rent Reaches 50% of All Transactions
key_headlines.summary: Seoul apartment rental market shows monthly rent now accounts for 50.8% of all apartment transactions for the first time, as jeonse (key money deposit) shortage forces renters to shift from traditional lease arrangements.

key_headlines.title: Global Central Banks Hold Rates Amid Middle East War Uncertainty
key_headlines.summary: The ECB and Bank of England both maintained interest rates as concerns over inflation and economic slowdown intensify following escalating Middle East tensions and oil price surges.

key_headlines.title: US Big Tech Giants Post Earnings Surprises Driven by AI Revenue Growth
key_headlines.summary: Major US technology companies including Google, Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon reported first-quarter earnings beats with cloud services and AI-driven advertising showing robust growth, validating AI investment profitability.

key_headlines.title: Q1 Card Approval Spending Reaches 322.1 Trillion Won, Up 7.2%
key_headlines.summary: Korea's first-quarter card spending surged 7.2% to 322.1 trillion won, driven by online shopping and travel pre-booking demand as consumer activity remains resilient.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's first-quarter card approval spending reached 322.1 trillion won, representing a 7.2% increase driven by online shopping and travel reservation demand. Seoul's apartment market shows continued price moderation with the Gangnam and Yongsan districts experiencing declines, while construction costs have risen for seven consecutive months amid Middle East conflict impacts. Korea's excess tax revenue from semiconductor supercycle and KOSPI record highs is contributing to increased government coffers, though fiscal reform remains a long-term priority. Currency weakness and geopolitical tensions continue to create economic uncertainty across major indicators.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The European Central Bank maintained its deposit rate at 2.00%, base rate at 2.15%, and marginal lending rate at 2.40% amid concerns that Middle East conflicts will increase inflationary pressures and economic headwinds. The Bank of England also held its base rate at 3.75% for the third consecutive time, adopting a wait-and-see approach regarding energy price shocks and inflation risks. The Federal Reserve maintained rates at 3.50% with three dissenting votes expressing concerns about the stance, representing notable internal disagreement rarely seen since 1992. South Korea's first-quarter tax revenues increased 16.7% to 108.8 trillion won compared to the prior year, driven by semiconductor supercycle and record stock market performance. Global policymakers are balancing persistent inflation concerns with economic growth uncertainties as oil prices surge.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI declined 1.38% to close at 6,598.87, surrendering the 6,600-point threshold amid international oil price spikes and hawkish rate hold rhetoric. Foreign investors sold 1.46 trillion won in shares while individuals and institutions made net purchases, indicating divergent market sentiment. Entertainment and real estate sectors led the decline, falling 2.30% and 1.44% respectively. The broader market showed technical weakness with KOSPI opening higher at 6,739.39 but unable to maintain gains as external uncertainty dominated trading. US stock markets also closed mixed due to oil price volatility despite generally positive earnings results from major tech companies.
sections.Industry & Technology: LG Energy Solution secured a landmark 10 trillion won contract to supply cylindrical batteries to BMW for its next-generation 'Neue Klasse' electric vehicle platform, with production planned at the Arizona facility. The company reported first-quarter 46-series cylindrical battery orders exceeding 100GWh with total order backlog surpassing 440GWh, signaling recovery in the EV battery market. Samsung SDI is also benefiting from renewed demand, having secured contracts with Mercedes-Benz for EV battery supply. Korean secondary battery makers are emerging from market challenges with new major customer acquisitions suggesting EV demand recovery. Energy storage system business expansion is providing additional growth avenues for battery manufacturers.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul apartment monthly rent transactions reached 50.8% of all apartment rentals in the first quarter, the highest proportion since statistics began in 2014, as jeonse shortages force renters to shift to monthly arrangements. Seoul's entire residential monthly rent transactions account for 70.5% of all lease agreements, reflecting severe jeonse market tightness stemming from reinforced owner-occupancy requirements. Apartment prices in Seoul showed slight moderation with continued declines in premium areas like Gangnam and Yongsan despite broader price increases. Developers are increasingly shifting to smaller 59-square-meter units instead of traditional 84-square-meter national standards to maximize profit margins and unit volumes. Real estate transactions increased 8.3% year-over-year in March despite housing affordability challenges.
sections.International Economy: Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell announced his intention to remain on the Fed Board of Governors after his term concludes, citing need to manage political pressures from the Trump administration and ensure central bank independence. The FOMC recorded unusual dissent with four members opposing the unanimous rate hold decision, the largest disagreement since 1992, reflecting divisions over policy direction amid geopolitical uncertainty. Powell criticized the Trump administration for dragging the Federal Reserve into political disputes while highlighting labor market weakness and maintaining inflation remains above target. The US economy continues to show resilience with steady economic activity, though job growth remains subdued and unemployment has remained essentially flat. Oil price surges from Middle East conflicts are creating upside inflation risks that complicate the Fed's policy outlook.
sections.AI & Economy: US major technology companies including Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon reported first-quarter earnings surprises, with cloud services and AI-driven advertising revenues showing exceptional growth that validates heavy AI infrastructure investments. Alphabet recorded its highest revenue growth rate in four years at 109.9 billion dollars, with cloud services driving the expansion as AI demand accelerates. Microsoft's revenue increased 18% to 82.9 billion dollars with cloud service Azure surging 40%, demonstrating AI monetization success across multiple platforms. South Korean tech company Naver achieved record first-quarter revenue of 3.24 trillion won with AI contributing over 50% of growth through its ADVoost advertising solution and integrated AI platform. The AI earnings surge has effectively dispelled early-2026 AI bubble concerns, though capital expenditure burdens remain a potential variable for sustained profitability.
sections.Others: Public institutions' debt ratio improved to 174.1%, down 6.4 percentage points year-over-year, while new hiring expanded by approximately 7,000 positions to 27,000 employees across 342 public agencies. The government plans comprehensive foreign worker management reforms transitioning from fragmented policies to integrated systems covering recruitment through residency, while easing workplace mobility restrictions under the employment permit system. Woori Bank organized a US investment briefing to support Korean companies' US expansion amid escalating Korea-US tariff negotiations and rising protectionism. Labor groups are accelerating wage negotiations and demanding performance bonuses as labor season approaches earlier this year. Stalled peace negotiations between the US and Iran show divergent positions, with the US seeking diplomatic agreements while Iran expresses distrust, creating continued geopolitical uncertainty affecting energy markets.
